schiner-henry-1516-06-14.summary: Cardinal Schiner at Trent to Henry VIII, 14 June 1516, while leading Maximilian's army in Italy on English money. The cipher holds the secret of the letter: Maximilian had offered Henry, through Schiner, the duchy of Milan and the succession to the Empire.
schiner-henry-1516-06-14.en:
Most Sacred [Majesty], etc. — From Your Majesty's most kind ⟦letter⟧ sent to me from London on the 8th of last month ⟦I
see that you take it ill that I have not⟧ offered Your Majesty anything of the course of events, of the outcome of
things and of the affairs of war, ⟦nor⟧ in full. Which indeed ⟦I regret; but with the utmost⟧ prayers I beg the same
⟦Majesty⟧ to deign to ⟦weigh⟧ the cause of this neglect. For from the day on which I set out from the Val di Sole to
the Imperial Majesty's ⟦camp, to direct⟧ the armies and the affairs of war, I never [had the means of writing] to Your
Majesty; [but, intent] on the remaining pending matters and on guarding against dangers, I at last reached [Verona]
safe, and having now come as far as here, I have stayed three days to speed certain ex[peditions].

snip.cap: Schiner to Henry VIII, 14 June 1516, as Büchi printed it: roman type was clear, italics were cipher (litteris video moleste ferre, quod nec …)
snip.credit: A. Büchi (ed.), Korrespondenzen und Akten zur Geschichte des Kardinals Matth. Schiner II (Basel 1925), p. 67; scan: Swiss National Library, e-Helvetica nbdig-59316

system: Words and phrases of a Latin letter written in cipher and set into clear text, with a monogram for 'Vestrae Majestati' (Brewer); the sign system is not known here, and Büchi printed no key.
